discovery_metadata.title: Oxygen‐Enriched Porous Carbon Derived from Biomass Waste for Supercapacitors with High Electrochemical Performances
discovery_metadata.abstract: The porous carbon derived biomass is inexpensive and eco-friendly, making them become the promising electrode materials for supercapacitors. In this work, oxygen-enriched porous carbon were derived from Platanus fibers via a carbonization and activation process using KMnO4 as activator. KMnO4 paly the roles of both activator and modifier. The obtained porous carbon not only possess high oxygen content but also show tube-like hollow structures. The sample OPF-3 exhibits a high oxygen content (13.79%), total pore volume (0.64 cm3 g-1) and specific surface area (1406 m2 g-1). The prepared OPF-3 electrode material presents a high specific capacitance (318 F g-1 at 0.5 A g-1) and retained 181 F g-1 even at 50 A g-1, in a three-electrode system. The as-prepared symmetric supercapacitors symmetric supercapacitors a high specific capacitance (252 F g-1) and an excellent cycle stability (96.5% specific capacitance retention after 20000 cycles). Furthermore, it has a high energy of 7.04 Wh kg-1 at a power density 22.66 W kg-1. This study provided a facile, inexpensive and environmentally method for biomass prepared to porous carbon, which used as electrode materials present excellent electrochemical performances.
